integrity_incident.finding: Prior Data Centers artifacts overstated whole-text verification and completion.
integrity_incident.treatment: Revoked artifacts may be used only as source-discovery and hypothesis scaffolds. Their admissions, passage analyses, saturation results, promotion decisions and COMPLETE status carry no authority.

last_useful_scaffold.limitation: Its 25 source records and notes are retained as candidates and hypotheses, not inherited admissions.

audit_contract.journal_gate: Current Journal Impact Factor >= 2.0, used only as a binary gate.
audit_contract.source_rule: Abstracts, snippets, search results, previews, metadata pages and partial text do not count as whole-text review.
audit_contract.blocked_rule: If every substantive section cannot be reviewed, mark the source audit-blocked and do not admit it.
audit_contract.extraction_rule: Inherited notes are hypotheses to confirm, rewrite, split or reject after reading; they cannot bootstrap admission.
audit_contract.saturation_rule: Only begins after recomputed conceptual coverage is complete; two consecutive five-paper challenges must each add <=2 genuinely new generalizable observations and reopen no material gap.
audit_contract.long_form_rule: Use only genuinely accessible academic texts; approximately 10–15 passage analyses after complete substantive reading.

candidate_population.title: Recalibrating global data center energy-use estimates
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: bottom-up global energy-accounting synthesis and policy forum

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The paper rejects traffic- or workload-only extrapolation, integrates equipment, virtualization, storage, network, PUE and market-structure data, and presents a conditional near-term efficiency scenario.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: Energy is decomposed across servers, storage, network equipment, and infrastructure; compute instances, IP traffic, storage capacity and electricity are separate quantities.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: From 2010 to 2018, estimated compute instances rose 550% while global data-center electricity rose about 6%, from roughly 194 to 205 TWh; energy per compute instance fell about 20% annually.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: The result depends on shifts from traditional facilities toward cloud and hyperscale sites, virtualization, device efficiency, storage density, and PUE; practical PUE improvement approaches a floor near highly optimized hyperscale operation.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: This is a bottom-up accounting synthesis and conditional near-term scenario, not proof that future AI load growth will remain energy-flat.
limitations: Public bottom-up data on facility types, locations, equipment and efficiency remain incomplete.
Long-run technical limits and disruptive technologies are uncertain.
The scenario requires continued efficiency progress and policy effort.
anti_patterns: Do not scale electricity directly from IP traffic, workload, storage or compute-instance growth.
Do not turn a conditional near-term plateau scenario into a permanent forecast.
Do not use PUE alone as a measure of useful computing service.

candidate_population.title: Data centre water consumption
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: critical review and measurement-framework analysis

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The article expands data-center environmental accounting beyond energy, separates direct cooling water from electricity-generation water, evaluates measurement metrics and disclosure gaps, and links water impact to local scarcity and siting.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: Withdrawal differs from consumption; site WUE differs from source-inclusive WUE; both divide water by IT-equipment energy and therefore depend on consistent site, time and grid boundaries.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: The article reports that a traditional 1 MW facility can consume around 25.5 million litres annually and that higher chilled-water temperatures can materially reduce cooling cost, but both figures are technology- and climate-conditioned.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Cooling demand and feasible technology vary with ambient climate, season, water source, electricity generation mix, facility design and equipment tolerance.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: The paper synthesizes published and corporate data; it does not estimate a universal causal effect of siting or cooling changes.
limitations: Operator water disclosure is sparse and often not attributed specifically to data centers.
Source-water intensity factors vary by technology and geography and become stale as grids change.
Customer migration to cloud can reduce visibility into the resources behind purchased services.
anti_patterns: Do not equate withdrawal with consumption.
Do not call site WUE a complete water footprint.
Do not compare vendor water totals without organizational and methodological boundaries.

candidate_population.title: Using life cycle assessment to drive innovation for sustainable cool clouds
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: provider-authored cradle-to-grave comparative life-cycle assessment

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The study defines a cradle-to-grave functional unit, compares three advanced cooling designs against air cooling, decomposes use-phase and embodied impacts, and uses the tradeoffs to inform early design choices.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: Impacts are annualized and normalized per virtual core; the boundary includes building shell, workload, servers, racks or tanks, support equipment, grid electricity, water, fluids and end-of-life treatment.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: The modeled advanced-cooling designs reduce GHG emissions by roughly 15–21%, primary energy by 15–20%, and blue-water consumption by 31–52% per virtual core-year against the modeled air-cooled reference.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Results shift with grid mix, server lifetime, density, cooling fluid, maintenance model, regulatory treatment, and whether use-phase or embodied impacts dominate.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: This comparative LCA estimates impacts under a specified provider design model; it is not measured fleet-wide realized savings or a market-adoption result.
limitations: Specific cooling-fluid, data-center-equipment and semiconductor inventories were missing or outdated and required proxies.
The paper uses a pedigree matrix rather than a complete quantitative uncertainty distribution.
Provider design assumptions and functional-unit choices condition transferability.
anti_patterns: Do not compare cooling systems without the same functional unit and life-cycle boundary.
Do not describe modeled per-core reductions as measured total-fleet reductions.
Do not ignore embodied burdens that become more prominent as operational electricity decarbonizes.

candidate_population.title: Decarbonising digital infrastructure and urban sustainability in the case of data centres
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: mixed-method urban infrastructure and sustainability case study

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The study challenges digital dematerialization, maps data-center growth into a land-, water- and carbon-constrained urban system, and identifies implementation gaps across technology, policy, finance, infrastructure and people.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: The evidence is a non-exhaustive asset landscape, policy and corporate documents, 59 semi-structured interviews, and two validation workshops totaling 150 participants.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: Counts describe the qualitative evidence base, not a representative estimate of all operators or projects.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Tropical climate, grid carbon, land and water scarcity, connectivity, sovereignty, financing, brownfield status and operator risk tolerance change feasible transitions.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: This is a mixed-method Singapore case, not a causal technology evaluation. Corporate claims and project projections remain stakeholder evidence.
limitations: The asset landscape is non-exhaustive.
The institutional and physical regime is Singapore-specific.
Cross-border relocation can shift rather than remove environmental burdens.
anti_patterns: Do not treat PUE, renewable certificates or a green-building label as complete sustainability.
Do not treat announced green finance as realized low-carbon infrastructure.
Do not infer regional burden reduction when restrictions displace capacity across a border.

candidate_population.title: Maximizing waste heat recovery from a building-integrated edge data center
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: physical pilot parameterization plus validated thermal simulation and workload-placement optimization

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The paper measures a pilot rack, validates a thermal model, searches workload placements with a fast evaluator, and reports modeled heat-recovery gains before delimiting operational deployment.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: A 32-server single-rack pilot supports up to 12 kW; optimization compares modeled placements against random placement under specified flow and load conditions.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: The fast evaluator reports R-squared 0.93 and RMSE 1.44 degrees C; the validated model estimates up to 17.1% more recovered heat and up to 53.2% lower transferred cooling load under selected conditions.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Benefits decline as IT load rises and placement flexibility disappears; geometry, hardware homogeneity, cooling configuration, workload colocation and thermal limits condition results.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: Physical measurements parameterize the model, but optimization gains are simulated rather than measured production-fleet energy savings.
limitations: Single-rack scale and homogeneous hardware.
No production scheduler deployment.
No measured net building or grid energy outcome.
anti_patterns: Do not collapse experimental parameterization, model validation, simulated policy gain and production deployment.
Do not call recovered heat net electricity savings.
Do not transfer low-load placement gains into saturation conditions.

candidate_population.title: Data center growth in the United States: Decoupling the demand for services from electricity use
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: twenty-year bottom-up United States stock-and-flow electricity model with scenarios

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The paper reconstructs equipment stocks and operational characteristics by space type, derives useful workload with full-power equivalents, and contrasts frozen-efficiency, current-trend and best-practice scenarios.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: Installed servers, full-power-equivalent workload, floor-space type, PUE, utilization and annual electricity are modeled separately; neither installed base nor electricity alone measures service demand.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: Recent United States data-center electricity demand was nearly steady around 70 billion kWh, while the same projected 2020 workload spans roughly 135 billion kWh between frozen-efficiency and best-practice scenarios and nearly a factor of four across the full scenario range.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Efficiency, virtualization and consolidation opportunities differ across server closets, rooms, localized facilities, mid-tier sites and hyperscale facilities.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: This is calibrated bottom-up accounting plus conditional scenarios, not a forecast that fixes post-2020 electricity demand.
limitations: Input data are uneven across space and equipment types.
Scenario outcomes depend on adoption rates for efficiency and consolidation.
The analysis does not establish post-2020 AI-specific demand.
anti_patterns: Do not equate installed servers with delivered workload.
Do not treat a scenario envelope as a point forecast.
Do not apply hyperscale efficiency to the whole heterogeneous stock.

candidate_population.title: Assessing the environmental impact of data centres part 1: Background, energy use and metrics
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: critical literature review of data-center energy, environmental impact and metrics

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The review traces why operational energy and PUE became dominant, evaluates later carbon, water and compute metrics, and shows why no single operational metric represents whole-system sustainability.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: PUE is total facility energy divided by IT-equipment energy; other metrics use different numerators, boundaries and service denominators and therefore are not interchangeable.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: Reported sector totals and facility ratios vary with inventory scope, time, site type and measurement practice; the review treats them as boundary-conditioned rather than universal constants.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Facilities range from single racks and server rooms to warehouse-scale sites, with different cooling, redundancy, occupancy and measurement feasibility.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: This is a critical review of metrics and evidence, not a measured intervention study.
limitations: The literature and disclosure base was incomplete and rapidly changing.
Single-issue metrics omit cross-impact and life-cycle effects.
Metric definitions and measurement points are not always harmonized.
anti_patterns: Do not call PUE a sustainability score.
Do not compare ratios without aligned boundaries and time periods.
Do not infer lower total impact from improvement in one operational metric.

candidate_population.title: Data Center Energy Evaluation Tool Development and Analysis of Power Usage Effectiveness with Different Economizer Types in Various Climate Zones
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: engineering-tool development and comparative climate/economizer simulation

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The study develops a reduced-input energy tool, verifies it against established simulation software, and uses it to compare PUE under cooling and economizer choices across climates.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: PUE is calculated from modeled IT and support energy under aligned weather, setpoint, load and cooling-system assumptions.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: Predicted PUE and cooling savings change materially with outdoor temperature and humidity, economizer type and control limits rather than inhering in the equipment label alone.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Air-side and water-side economizers have different feasible hours and performance across climate zones and setpoints.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: Software agreement verifies implementation consistency; it is not field validation of realized annual operating cost or environmental impact.
limitations: Capital cost and maintenance are excluded.
Water use and heat-reuse value are excluded.
The modeled system does not cover all liquid-cooling or rear-door configurations.
anti_patterns: Do not generalize an economizer result across climates.
Do not treat software-to-software agreement as production validation.
Do not infer whole-system sustainability from modeled PUE.

candidate_population.title: Thermal Performance Evaluation of a Data Center Cooling System under Fault Conditions
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: project-specific transient thermal analysis and commissioning-oriented fault evaluation

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The study models loss-of-cooling faults in an actual 20 MW project configuration and translates transient temperature behavior into backup activation and commissioning requirements.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: The key outcome is time until server-inlet temperature exceeds the specified allowable envelope under defined chilled-water and supply-air starting conditions.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: At chilled-water/supply-air conditions no higher than about 17/24 degrees C, allowable time was about 320 seconds; warmer initial conditions caused faster temperature rise, supporting backup activation within 300 seconds.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Thermal ride-through depends on starting temperature, air volume, thermal mass, fault type, redundancy and whether cooling components share UPS protection.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: The project geometry is real, but fault outcomes are transient simulations used for design and commissioning rather than measured fleet outage statistics.
limitations: Results depend on the studied 20 MW configuration.
Model assumptions govern thermal mass and airflow response.
The study evaluates a bounded fault interval, not long-duration resilience.
anti_patterns: Do not call installed redundancy verified resilience before integrated fault testing.
Do not transfer a ride-through time across thermal starting states.
Do not assume IT UPS protection also protects cooling.

candidate_population.title: The Energy-Saving Potential of Air-Side Economisers in Modular Data Centres: Analysis of Opportunities and Risks in Different Climates
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: dynamic simulation of a modular data center across four climate regimes

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The paper models an air-side economizer for a 90 kW modular facility and tests its opportunity and risk under four distinct climates.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: Energy savings and PUE are annual modeled outcomes relative to the same mechanical-cooling base case and specified control envelope.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: The model estimates savings as high as about 86% in a favorable moderate climate, while hot-dry and hot-humid climates provide much smaller opportunities.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Temperature, humidity, enthalpy, particulate risk, control strategy and climate determine free-cooling hours and suitability.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: The base model is checked against published PUE data, but climate comparisons remain simulations rather than multi-site billing measurements.
limitations: Validation lacks detailed facility billing and infiltration measurements.
Contaminant and reliability risks are not fully quantified.
The 90 kW modular geometry is not a hyperscale campus.
anti_patterns: Do not apply the maximum modeled saving to all climates.
Do not equate a modular prototype with fleet-average performance.
Do not omit air-quality and humidity constraints from free-cooling claims.

candidate_population.title: Flexibility-Based Energy and Demand Management in Data Centers: A Case Study for Cloud Computing
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: flexibility review, management-framework design and lab-grade cloud testbed experiment

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The paper separates kWh minimization from kW peak reduction, maps technical flexibility to contracts, implements management systems, and evaluates them on a lab-grade cloud testbed.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: Overall energy and interval peak power are different objectives; flexibility is the feasible, time-bounded change subject to workload, hardware and SLA constraints.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: The reported case results include roughly 33% overall energy saving and 50% demand-response peak reduction under the tested federation and workload conditions.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Deferrability, migration, consolidation, thermal headroom, storage state, workload shape and contract terms determine deliverable flexibility.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: The control mechanisms are experimentally evaluated at lab-grade scale; federation-wide savings are not evidence of unrestricted production-fleet response.
limitations: Lab-grade scale limits external validity.
Savings depend on workload and baseline construction.
QoS and contractual acceptability constrain response.
anti_patterns: Do not equate nameplate load with dispatchable flexibility.
Do not conflate kW peak reduction with kWh energy savings.
Do not ignore SLA and workload consequences.

candidate_population.title: Data Centers Optimized Integration with Multi-Energy Grids: Test Cases and Results in Operational Environment
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: multi-site operational pilots and test cases for electrical, thermal and IT flexibility

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The study implements a flexibility-management architecture and demonstrates separate electrical, thermal and workload scenarios in operational pilots and test cases.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: Electrical load, recoverable heat and movable IT work are separate profiles; reported flexibility is scenario- and interval-specific.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: The test cases show that renewable availability can be coupled to storage and load migration, but the achievable level changes with QoS and production conditions.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: On-site generation, battery state, workload mobility, network delay, heat demand and site topology change the feasible response.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: Operational pilots establish technical feasibility at their tested scale, not a universal market-wide flexibility quantity.
limitations: Pilot and micro-data-center scales are not full campus deployments.
Economic and regulatory participation conditions vary by market.
Heat-reuse results require a coincident local sink.
anti_patterns: Do not add electrical, thermal and IT flexibility as if they were identical units.
Do not call available waste heat useful heat without a matched sink.
Do not extrapolate pilot response to nameplate campus load.

candidate_population.title: How Data Centers Have Come to Matter: Governing the Spatial and Environmental Footprint of the 'Digital Gateway to Europe'
candidate_population.journal: International Journal of Urban and Regional Research
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: qualitative urban-infrastructure and policy-history case study

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The paper traces how a spatially concentrated data-center sector moved from politically obscured enabling infrastructure to contested land, power and heat infrastructure, followed by moratoria and policy reform.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: The unit of analysis is a metropolitan governance regime and its clustered campuses, institutions and policy fields, not a national facility census.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: Facility counts, campus maps and policy events support the historical case; they do not estimate a general causal effect of data-center entry.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Local grid scarcity, land constraints, municipal competition, national policy, connectivity and heat-network institutions determine the governance response.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: Process tracing supports a contextual account of politicization and regulation, not a transportable numerical treatment effect.
limitations: Amsterdam is an unusually mature and concentrated gateway market.
Policy documents and interviews reflect institutional perspectives.
The case cannot serve as a global fleet inventory.
anti_patterns: Do not describe cloud infrastructure as placeless.
Do not infer national capacity from one metropolitan cluster.
Do not count planned heat reuse as delivered heat without network and demand realization.

candidate_population.title: The environmental footprint of data centers in the United States
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: bottom-up geospatial operational water and carbon footprint model

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The study links facilities to grids, power plants, water utilities, wastewater treatment and watersheds to estimate location-specific operational water and carbon footprints and siting tradeoffs.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: Direct cooling water, indirect power-generation water, water-treatment energy and GHG emissions are attributed through explicit operational boundaries; a hypothetical 1 MW site is used for comparable siting intensities.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: About one-fifth of servers direct water footprint is in moderately to highly water-stressed watersheds, nearly half are at least partly powered by plants in water-stressed regions, and modeled 2018 operations account for about 31.5 million tons CO2-equivalent, around 0.5% of United States emissions.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Grid mix, watershed stress, cooling practice, utility territory and facility location produce large geographic variation and tradeoffs among water, scarcity-weighted water and carbon.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: This is spatial attribution and counterfactual siting analysis, not observation of identical facilities randomly relocated.
limitations: Facility locations and server counts are coverage-limited inputs.
Grid and utility attribution uses modeled connections and averages.
Operational scope excludes full embodied and construction impacts.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a mapped facility list as a complete fleet census.
Do not report national averages as local burden.
Do not equate ordinary water volume with scarcity-weighted impact.

candidate_population.title: A Circular Economy for the Data Centre Industry: Using Design Methods to Address the Challenge of Whole System Sustainability in a Unique Industrial Sector
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: project case study using sector survey, nine expert interviews and design-process evaluation

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The paper frames the data-center equipment chain as ten siloed subsectors, applies whole-system design methods in CEDaCI, and evaluates early project engagement and perceived impact through a 44-person survey and nine senior-expert interviews.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: Evidence measures participant engagement, perceptions and project-process outputs; it does not measure sector-wide recovered material or avoided lifecycle impact.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: The empirical evaluation includes 44 survey participants and nine senior experts, with 17 interview themes; authors explicitly state that creating a sectoral circular economy in three and a half years is unrealistic.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Designers, manufacturers, operators, users, refurbishers, asset-disposition firms and recyclers have different information, incentives and technical constraints.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: The evidence supports early awareness, engagement and design-process learning, not proof of completed industry transformation.
limitations: Small, project-engaged samples risk positive-selection bias.
Outcomes are early-stage and largely process or perception measures.
Material-flow and avoided-impact outcomes were not yet observed sector-wide.
anti_patterns: Do not call project participation completed circularity.
Do not infer recovered material from design-tool availability.
Do not optimize one lifecycle stage without tracing effects on the other subsectors.

candidate_population.title: Environmental footprints of the data center service sector in Sweden
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: national footprint model plus GIS multi-criteria site-suitability analysis

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The study constructs a Swedish data-center inventory from heterogeneous public and survey sources, estimates sector energy, water and GHG footprints, then scores existing and prospective locations with a multi-criteria GIS tool.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: Facility environmental estimates and the site-suitability index are separate outputs; the latter combines renewable access, free cooling, excess-heat receivers and resilience to water shortage.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: The model estimates roughly 5.4% of Swedish electricity, 42 million cubic metres of annual water and 0.3% of national GHG emissions for the sector; 68 facilities score at or below 45% on the authors site-suitability index.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Northern and southern locations differ in climate, geology, grid, heat sinks and water risk, while missing facility data require proxies.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: This is inventory estimation and suitability scoring, not causal evidence that relocating a facility produces the modeled benefit.
limitations: The facility inventory is assembled from questionnaires, permits, corporate sites and open repositories rather than mandatory standardized reporting.
Missing facility parameters require assumptions and imputation.
A composite suitability score inherits selected criteria and weights.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the assembled list as a certified fleet census.
Do not read a suitability score as actual operating performance.
Do not compare composite scores without preserving criteria and weights.

candidate_population.title: Planning data center locations in Swedish municipalities: A comparative case study of Luleå and Stockholm
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: comparative urban-planning case study

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The paper compares how two municipalities integrate data centers into spatial and energy planning and identifies determinants of municipal adaptive capacity.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: The unit of analysis is the municipal energy-spatial system; determinants include electricity and water infrastructure, heat-producer and user diversity, land-use diversity and property fragmentation.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: The result is a structured comparative judgment that Stockholm exhibits higher adaptive capacity than Luleå, not a causal effect size or universal location ranking.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Climate, energy availability, ownership fragmentation, district-heating institutions and municipal authority change feasible integration.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: Comparative case evidence supports planning mechanisms and contrasts, not a general causal ranking of all municipalities.
limitations: Two Swedish municipalities limit transferability.
Planning evidence does not itself establish completed infrastructure or realized heat exchange.
Adaptive-capacity assessment depends on the selected framework and evidence.
anti_patterns: Do not equate municipal plan adoption with energized capacity.
Do not call waste heat beneficial without an integrated user and network.
Do not rank sites on climate alone while ignoring governance and infrastructure.

candidate_population.title: The relationship between data centers and the climate is a systems challenge: a spatial analysis of United States data centers
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: national geospatial operational-risk analysis

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The paper combines a coverage-limited site inventory with heat, water-stress and grid-emissions layers to evaluate environment-to-facility operational risks and facility-to-environment burdens.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: The analysis locates more than 2,400 facilities and attaches regional environmental-risk indicators; site presence does not encode MW, operating state or utilization.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: Spatial clusters and risk categories reveal that many facilities face heat or water stress and materially different grid emissions, but the paper does not convert site counts into fleet load.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Local climate, watershed conditions, grid mix and regional clustering jointly determine risk; those variables can be correlated rather than independent.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: This is cross-sectional spatial association and risk screening, not causal impact evaluation.
limitations: Commercial and public facility inventories may omit, duplicate or misclassify sites.
Location-only records lack standardized capacity and operating state.
Regional indicators do not substitute for facility operating measurements.
anti_patterns: Do not multiply site counts by a generic MW value.
Do not call proximity to risk realized outage or damage.
Do not infer causation from spatial clustering.

candidate_population.title: Data centres as a source of flexibility for power systems
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: critical review and case-based flexibility synthesis

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The review maps data-center assets and workload controls to power-system services and tests their plausibility against case examples and market requirements.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: Flexibility must specify direction, response time, duration, recovery, energy capacity, availability window and service baseline; asset capacity is not automatically deliverable response.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: Case values vary by asset and market and are presented as examples rather than a fleet aggregate; the authors report no new dataset for the review itself.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: UPS topology, battery sizing, generator rules, workload type, QoS/SLA, electricity-market design and regulation change availability.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: The review supports technical potential and bounded case feasibility, not a measured national dispatchable total.
limitations: No new data were used.
Case studies are heterogeneous and may be selectively reported.
Regulatory and market transferability is limited.
anti_patterns: Do not sum all asset ratings as simultaneous flexibility.
Do not omit response duration and recovery.
Do not treat technical potential as market-qualified availability.

candidate_population.title: A Review of Data Centers Energy Consumption and Reliability Modeling
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: systematic technical review of component energy and reliability models

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The review classifies component energy models and analytical or simulation reliability methods across 193 papers, then identifies missing power-conditioning, cooling-reliability and failure-data evidence.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: Component power consumption, component reliability, degraded operation, service availability and tier classification are different model layers.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: Internal power-conditioning losses can approach 10% in cited configurations, but the review emphasizes that parameter availability can matter more than nominal model accuracy for usable assessment.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Topology, redundancy, component dependence, repair assumptions, cooling architecture and failure data determine modeled reliability.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: This is a model-taxonomy and research-gap review, not measured failure-rate estimation for the data-center fleet.
limitations: Failure data are scarce, particularly for cooling and component dependencies.
Reviewed models use inconsistent assumptions and validation.
Tier labels do not fully specify operating or degraded-state behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not equate tier classification with measured availability.
Do not assume independent component failures where systems are coupled.
Do not optimize energy without testing reliability consequences.

candidate_population.title: Sources of data center energy estimates: A comprehensive review
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: systematic provenance and methodology review of energy estimates

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The review traces original energy estimates rather than repeated citations, classifies their methods and boundaries, and evaluates how methodological opacity propagates divergent public claims.
inherited_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: Energy estimates differ by included facility types, equipment, geography, year, electricity boundary, workload proxy and whether the value is observed, modeled or forecast.
inherited_extraction.quantitative_behavior: Only 31% of reviewed sources were peer-reviewed publications and 38% were non-peer-reviewed reports; many sources did not disclose enough method to reproduce or compare estimates.
inherited_extraction.heterogeneity_and_regime: Global and national estimates rely on different mixtures of direct measurement, installed-stock models, traffic proxies and scenario assumptions.
inherited_extraction.causal_calibration: This is evidence-provenance analysis; it does not select a timeless correct energy total.
limitations: The review is bounded to original estimates located for 2007–2021.
Commercial and confidential sources limit validation.
Published methods and classifications can become stale as facility mix changes.
anti_patterns: Do not cite a secondary repetition as independent evidence.
Do not compare totals without reconstructing their scope and year.
Do not average incompatible estimates to manufacture precision.

candidate_population.title: Building Accurate Energy-Use Statistics for Data Centers
candidate_population.inherited_study_type_hypothesis: measurement-framework and policy analysis

inherited_extraction.claim_path: The paper diagnoses structural gaps in data-center energy statistics and proposes treating data centers as a distinct end-use sector with standardized, coordinated reporting.

verified_extraction.claim_path: A 32-server air-cooled edge rack is experimentally characterized; a fast thermal evaluator and a conjugate heat-transfer model are validated; a thermal-aware placement algorithm is then compared with random placement in simulation.
verified_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: The pilot rack supports up to 12 kW. Outcomes distinguish recovered heat, heat-exchanger transfer, outlet temperatures and cooling load under specified IT loads, airflow and water-flow conditions; none is automatically net building electricity savings.
verified_extraction.quantitative_behavior: The fast evaluator achieved RMSE 1.44 degrees C, MAE 1.09 degrees C and R-squared 0.93, with a statistically significant mean bias of 1.06 degrees C. The paper reports up to 17.1% greater recovered heat at 3 kW, at least 8% above 50% capacity, 14.6% cooling-load reduction from workload allocation, and up to 53.2% in the combined optimized case; gains approach zero at full utilization.

verified_extraction.claim_path: DCSim dynamically models IT, cooling and auxiliary power under baseline, direct air-side, indirect air-side and water-side economizer logic, is checked against DesignBuilder’s EnergyPlus implementation, and is used for conditional design comparisons across ASHRAE climate zones.
verified_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: Hourly and annual PUE equal modeled total facility power divided by IT power. The study also reports cooling-energy components, operating-mode hours, relative annual cooling energy and PUE distributions; these remain modeled design outcomes.
verified_extraction.quantitative_behavior: Software-to-software hourly CVRMSE was 0-9.3% for the baseline equipment components and 1.4-10.75% for the air-side-economizer case. verified_extraction.claim_path: The study maps the cooling configuration of a 20 MW data-centre project, models server-inlet temperatures under normal and six fault conditions with CFD, and combines those outputs with chilled-water inventory and thermal-capacity equations to estimate cooling ride-through time.
verified_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: The relevant outcomes are server-inlet air temperature, CRAH supply air and chilled-water temperatures, coil capacity, 45 cubic metres of pipe water per typical floor, and elapsed seconds after cooling loss. The study does not estimate annual PUE or net energy savings.
verified_extraction.quantitative_behavior: With chilled-water supply at or below 17 degrees C, CRAH supply air at or below 24 degrees C and modeled coil capacity of 85%, server inlet air stayed within the ASHRAE 18-27 degrees C range for about 320 seconds. verified_extraction.claim_path: The paper instantiates a standalone 90-kW modular data-centre specification in EnergyPlus, holds design and IT load constant, varies weather across four cities, and compares mechanical cooling with a dry-bulb-controlled air-side economizer.
verified_extraction.measurement_and_denominator: The modeled process heat load is 90 kW or 2,150 W per square metre, constant 24/7. Outcomes are annual cooling electricity and PUE under a COP of 3.0, a 24 degrees C cooling setpoint, 30-50% relative-humidity band and a 5% allowance for economizer actuators and sensors.

These are modeled cooling-electricity deltas for one configuration, not total-facility field savings.

Aggregate PUE values from Stockholm and Dubai provide calibration targets; San Francisco and Singapore use an assumed 1.5 benchmark rather than site observations. Validation uses aggregate PUE values rather than hourly component-level billing and thermal data; the Stockholm divergence is 9%.
San Francisco and Singapore lack empirical site PUE and are compared with an assumed reference benchmark.
The selected differential dry-bulb control does not resolve full enthalpy, contaminant, filtration or humidification/dehumidification trade-offs.
The paper prints the PUE equation as IT load divided by total facility load even though reported values use the conventional greater-than-one direction; the equation label is internally inconsistent.
No capital cost, water, carbon, reliability or hardware-contamination outcome is evaluated.

long_form_passage_analyses.analytical_job: turn disagreement among published energy estimates into a research object before trying to resolve it

observations.observation: Disagreement among estimates is itself evidence about boundaries, methods, and source dependence and should be characterized before selecting a preferred number.
A strong opening connects estimation uncertainty to the decisions it can distort, then states the exact comparison the analysis will perform.

stylistic_notes: opens with consequence rather than a literature list
uses disparity to motivate method inspection
does not promise a single context-free correct estimate

long_form_passage_analyses.location: Review methodology: eligibility, normalization, and provenance tracing
long_form_passage_analyses.analytical_job: define which claims are comparable and how reported estimates are followed to their first-level sources
structure: normalize time and units where defensible

observations.observation: Eligibility criteria determine the class of claim a review can make; publication counts, estimate counts, and independent evidence counts must remain distinct.
Normalization should make comparable quantities legible without erasing incompatible temporal, geographic, or system boundaries.

stylistic_notes: method choices precede the results they enable
unit harmonization is paired with boundary warnings
provenance tracing is described as an auditable operation

long_form_passage_analyses.location: Bringing estimates together and identifying key source classes
long_form_passage_analyses.analytical_job: report the evidence base descriptively before interpreting why estimates diverge
structure: defer mechanism claims until the evidence map is visible

observations.observation: Coverage, estimate counts, and denominator choices should be reported before narrative interpretation so readers can see what the synthesis actually represents.
Repeated use of the same upstream dataset creates correlated evidence, so apparent publication abundance cannot be treated as equivalent to independent measurement.

stylistic_notes: descriptive inventory comes before adjudication
counts are attached to defined objects
source recurrence is visualized as evidence structure rather than relegated to a caveat

long_form_passage_analyses.location: Method taxonomy and interrogation of estimation assumptions
long_form_passage_analyses.analytical_job: compare bottom-up, top-down, and extrapolative estimates through their assumptions and failure modes
structure: identify what each method observes versus imputes

observations.observation: A method taxonomy becomes analytically useful only when each class is paired with its data requirements, assumptions, blind spots, and characteristic failure modes.
Extrapolation inherits both the uncertainty and the boundary choices of its baseline; multiplication does not create independent evidence.

stylistic_notes: comparison is organized by analytical behavior rather than author
assumptions are interrogated symmetrically
critique distinguishes invalid logic from merely uncertain inputs

long_form_passage_analyses.location: Data quality, transparency, and hidden source chains
long_form_passage_analyses.analytical_job: show how incomplete disclosure and shared provenance constrain confidence
structure: separate source absence from source invalidity
translate transparency limits into confidence limits

observations.observation: Provenance mapping can reveal correlated error and apparent replication built on shared upstream estimates even when downstream publications look independent.
A source that is unavailable today should be labeled unverified or unavailable, not retroactively declared invalid without additional evidence.

stylistic_notes: transparency failures are quantified where possible
absence and falsity are not conflated
confidence statements follow the traceability evidence

long_form_passage_analyses.location: Technological change and the fragility of forward estimates
long_form_passage_analyses.analytical_job: separate parameter uncertainty from structural change in technology, utilization, and demand
structure: show why historical relationships may break
distinguish known unknowns from unmodeled change

observations.observation: Parameter uncertainty within a fixed model is different from structural uncertainty caused by changes in hardware, software, utilization, facility design, and demand composition.
Long-horizon scenarios should state monitoring variables and revision triggers rather than present a distant point estimate as a stable forecast.

stylistic_notes: uncertainty is decomposed rather than invoked generically
technology is treated as a changing structure, not a residual
the passage closes with conditions for updating claims

long_form_passage_analyses.analytical_job: translate the review into actor-specific actions while preserving uncertainty and side effects
structure: assign actions to data holders and researchers

observations.observation: Recommendations are more credible when assigned to actors with the data, authority, and incentives needed to execute them.
A conclusion should preserve foreseeable unintended consequences and implementation limits instead of converting a bounded evidence review into an unconditional policy prescription.

stylistic_notes: recommendations are grouped by actor
the conclusion returns to the opening estimation problem
uncertainty qualifies action without becoming an excuse for inaction

long_form_passage_analyses.location: Framing, research questions, and base scenario architecture
long_form_passage_analyses.analytical_job: construct a scenario ladder that separates baseline, bounds, and counterfactual interventions

observations.observation: A scenario ladder should distinguish base assumptions, uncertainty bounds, and intervention counterfactuals because each supports a different inference.
Explicit research questions should precede model outputs so the reader can distinguish planned comparisons from post hoc emphasis.

stylistic_notes: questions organize the paper before result magnitude
scenario labels encode analytical purpose
growth assumptions are presented as inputs rather than observations

long_form_passage_analyses.analytical_job: propagate each intervention through electricity, carbon, and water outcomes while preserving physical limits and rebound risk

observations.observation: An intervention should be carried through every modeled outcome it can affect because a gain on one axis can worsen or leave unchanged another axis.
A unit-efficiency improvement does not establish an aggregate reduction when adoption, service volume, utilization, or rebound changes concurrently.

stylistic_notes: mechanism precedes result
the same counterfactual is evaluated on multiple axes
percent improvement is not confused with a total-demand forecast

long_form_passage_analyses.location: Spatial distribution, grid mix, and multiobjective siting
long_form_passage_analyses.analytical_job: expose geographic trade-offs among carbon, direct water, indirect water, and infrastructure constraints
structure: join location to grid and water conditions

observations.observation: Multiobjective siting analysis must expose trade-offs among carbon, water, reliability, and infrastructure constraints rather than compress them into a single unexplained rank.
A location can improve one footprint through its resource mix while worsening another; the explanatory mechanism must accompany the geographic comparison.

stylistic_notes: maps are interpreted through resource mechanisms
no geography is labeled universally optimal
direct and electricity-mediated water remain separate

long_form_passage_analyses.location: Net-zero pathways, residual burdens, and sensitivity analysis
long_form_passage_analyses.analytical_job: evaluate how much physical burden remains after best-practice reductions and what is deferred to offsets or restoration

observations.observation: Mitigation claims should report the residual absolute burden after percentage reductions, especially under rapid baseline growth.
Physical reduction, renewable procurement, offsets, and water restoration are distinct mechanisms and should not be collapsed into a single net-zero label.

stylistic_notes: residuals are made visible after large percentage improvements
sensitivity is tied to decision-relevant parameters
compensation mechanisms are kept conceptually separate

long_form_passage_analyses.location: Discussion: implementation, local conditions, and governance
long_form_passage_analyses.analytical_job: translate model counterfactuals into implementable actions with infrastructure and governance preconditions

observations.observation: Policy recommendations should name the grid, water, permitting, data, and coordination preconditions on which modeled benefits depend.
Aggregate environmental improvement does not establish local benefit; distribution across communities and jurisdictions requires separate evidence.

stylistic_notes: discussion translates model quantities into institutional requirements
local effects are not inferred from national totals
recommendations retain feasibility conditions

long_form_passage_analyses.location: Methods: capacity projection and server-power chain
long_form_passage_analyses.analytical_job: make the causal and measurement chain from supply bottleneck to electricity demand inspectable parameter by parameter

observations.observation: A load projection should expose each transformation from bottleneck or shipment assumptions through rated power, utilization, operating time, facility overhead, and aggregate electricity.
Parameter-chain transparency lets disagreement attach to a specific conversion rather than to the model as an undifferentiated whole.

stylistic_notes: equations mirror the physical accounting chain
assumptions are placed near the conversion they control
rated power and realized load remain separate

long_form_passage_analyses.location: Methods and limitations: footprint scopes and uncertainty boundaries

Unmodeled uncertainties should be categorized explicitly—data, structural, behavioral, spatial, or policy—rather than hidden behind a generic limitations sentence.

stylistic_notes: boundary definitions precede totals
modeled and unmodeled uncertainty are separated

normalized_domain_synthesis.project_pipeline_and_capacity: Capacity is a stateful chain from proposal through delivered service. Nameplate power, contracted power, energized capacity, IT load, occupied capacity, utilization, and useful service are not interchangeable. Aggregate claims must identify both the state and denominator.
normalized_domain_synthesis.measurement_and_registry_architecture: Fleet estimates inherit registry coverage, source dependence, boundary choices, missingness, and temporal alignment. Repeated downstream citation of a shared upstream estimate is correlated evidence, not independent validation.
normalized_domain_synthesis.siting_and_geographic_burden: Siting jointly conditions grid carbon, direct and indirect water, land, network performance, infrastructure availability, reliability, and community exposure. An improvement can migrate burden across resource, subsystem, time, or jurisdiction.
normalized_domain_synthesis.energy_and_environment: Electricity, carbon, water, and lifecycle impacts must be modeled with explicit scopes and physical accounting chains. Percentage efficiency improvements do not determine absolute burden under changing scale, utilization, or workload composition.
normalized_domain_synthesis.thermal_and_water_systems: Cooling performance depends on climate, facility design, load profile, operating controls, water source, and heat-reuse sink. Modeled or demonstrated thermodynamic potential is not realized benefit without commissioning, integration, adoption, and stable operation.
normalized_domain_synthesis.reliability_and_flexibility: Redundancy and headroom are reliability resources, not automatically waste. Dispatchable flexibility is the feasible time-bounded change after workload, SLA, topology, storage, recovery, and thermal constraints—not installed load.
normalized_domain_synthesis.unit_efficiency_and_aggregate_demand: Lower resource intensity per compute or service unit can coexist with higher total infrastructure demand. Volume, density, service quality, adoption, utilization, hardware turnover, and rebound must remain explicit.
normalized_domain_synthesis.evidence_calibration: Scenario models, reviews, engineering simulations, lab experiments, pilots, inventories, governance studies, and research agendas support different inference classes. Findings are not promoted beyond the design, geography, scale, or outcome actually observed.
disallowed_inferences: Do not equate announced MW with energized, occupied, utilized, or service-delivering capacity.
Do not infer total electricity directly from traffic, compute, shipment, or rated-power growth without the intervening parameter chain.
Do not treat PUE, WUE, utilization, carbon intensity, and lifecycle functional units as interchangeable efficiency measures.
Do not infer aggregate reduction from a unit-efficiency improvement without scale and rebound analysis.
Do not infer local benefit from national or fleet-average environmental improvement.
Do not treat repeated citations of a common upstream estimate as independent corroboration.
Do not convert modeled, laboratory, or pilot potential into production-scale realized performance.
Do not collapse physical reduction, procurement instruments, offsets, and restoration into one undifferentiated net claim.
